records.claim: Damian Green was born on 17 January 1956.
Damian Green was born in Barry, Vale of Glamorgan, Wales.
Damian Green is a member of the Conservative political party.
Damian Green's spouse is Alicia Collinson.
Damian Green attended Balliol College, Oxford.

records.source_span: a member of the Culture, Media and Sport select committee from 1997 until his appointment to the frontbench by William Hague in 1998
records.value: Culture, Media and Sport select committee
records.claim: Damian Green was a member of the Culture, Media and Sport select committee from 1997 to 1998.

records.source_span: appointment to the frontbench by William Hague in 1998 as a spokesman on education and employment
records.claim: Damian Green was appointed as a spokesman on education and employment in 1998.

records.source_span: He spoke on the environment from 1999
records.claim: Damian Green was a spokesman on the environment from 1999.

records.source_span: promoted to the Shadow Cabinet by Iain Duncan Smith in 2001 as the Shadow Secretary of State for Education and Skills
records.value: Shadow Secretary of State for Education and Skills
records.claim: Damian Green was promoted to Shadow Secretary of State for Education and Skills in 2001.

records.source_span: In 2003, Michael Howard gave him the position of Shadow Secretary of State for Transport
records.value: Shadow Secretary of State for Transport
records.claim: Damian Green was given the position of Shadow Secretary of State for Transport in 2003.

records.source_span: In September 2004, he left the front bench altogether of his own accord and joined the home affairs select committee
records.value: member of home affairs select committee
records.claim: Damian Green left the front bench in September 2004 and joined the home affairs select committee.

records.source_span: has been a member of the treasury committee since the 2005 General Election
records.claim: Damian Green has been a member of the treasury committee since the 2005 General Election.

records.source_span: He returned to the frontbench under the leadership of David Cameron in 2005 as a spokesman on home affairs and shadow minister for immigration
records.value: spokesman on home affairs and shadow minister for immigration
records.claim: Damian Green returned to the frontbench in 2005 as a spokesman on home affairs and shadow minister for immigration.

records.source_span: He was the Minister of State for Police and Criminal Justice until 14 July 2014
records.value: Minister of State for Police and Criminal Justice
records.claim: Damian Green was the Minister of State for Police and Criminal Justice until 14 July 2014.

records.source_span: He was appointed as Secretary of State for Work and Pensions by Prime Minister Theresa May in July 2016
records.value: Secretary of State for Work and Pensions
records.claim: Damian Green was appointed as Secretary of State for Work and Pensions in July 2016.
